questions.questionText: Who is known as the developer of the C programming language?
questions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed the C programming language at Bell Laboratories in the early 1970s.

questions.questionText: Which symbol is used to terminate a statement in C?
questions.explanation: A semicolon (;) is used to terminate most statements in C.

questions.questionText: Which header file is commonly required for using printf() and scanf()?
questions.explanation: The stdio.h header file contains declarations for standard input and output functions such as printf() and scanf().

questions.questionText: Which function is the starting point of a standard C program?
questions.explanation: Execution of a standard C program begins from the main() function.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a valid identifier in C?
questions.explanation: An identifier can contain letters, digits and underscores, but it cannot begin with a digit or be a keyword.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a C keyword?
questions.explanation: int is a reserved keyword in C used to declare integer variables.

questions.questionText: Which data type is used to store a single character in C?
questions.explanation: The char data type is used to store a single character.

questions.questionText: Which data type is generally used to store decimal numbers in C?
questions.explanation: The float data type is commonly used to store numbers with fractional parts.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to declare a constant variable in C?
questions.explanation: The const keyword specifies that the value of a variable should not be modified after initialization.

questions.questionText: Which format specifier is commonly used with printf() to display an integer?
questions.explanation: %d is commonly used to display an integer value in decimal notation.

questions.questionText: Which format specifier is used to read a character using scanf()?
questions.explanation: The %c format specifier is used to read a single character.

questions.questionText: What is the result of 10 / 3 when both operands are integers in C?
questions.explanation: When both operands are integers, integer division is performed and the fractional part is discarded.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to find the remainder of an integer division?
questions.explanation: The modulus operator (%) returns the remainder after integer division.

questions.questionText: What is the value of x after executing int x = 5 + 3 * 2;?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so 3 * 2 is evaluated first. Therefore x = 5 + 6 = 11.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used for assignment in C?
questions.explanation: The = operator assigns the value on its right to the variable on its left.

questions.questionText: Which operator is used to compare two values for equality?
questions.explanation: The == operator checks whether two values are equal.

questions.questionText: Which statement is used to make a decision based on a condition?
questions.explanation: The if statement executes a block of code when its condition is true.

questions.questionText: What will be the output of the following code? int x = 10; if (x > 5) printf("Yes"); else printf("No");
questions.explanation: Since x is 10 and 10 > 5 is true, the if block executes and prints Yes.

questions.questionText: Which loop is generally suitable when the number of iterations is known in advance?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used when initialization, condition and update can be specified together.

questions.questionText: How many times will the following loop execute? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++)
questions.explanation: The values of i are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, so the loop executes 5 times.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to exit from a loop immediately?
questions.explanation: The break statement immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch statement.

questions.questionText: Which keyword skips the remaining statements of the current loop iteration and starts the next iteration?
questions.explanation: The continue statement skips the remaining part of the current iteration and proceeds with the next iteration.

questions.questionText: Which declaration correctly creates an integer array capable of storing 5 elements?
questions.explanation: The declaration int a[5]; creates an integer array with 5 elements indexed from 0 to 4.

questions.questionText: What is the index of the first element of an array in C?
questions.explanation: C arrays use zero-based indexing, so the first element is at index 0.

questions.questionText: Which character marks the end of a C string?
questions.explanation: A C string is terminated by the null character '\0'.
